text: For a functional φ, this linear map sends m to Σφ(m₀)m₁ when ρ(m)=Σm₀⊗m₁. Choosing φ to be a basis coordinate recovers the coefficient entries in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The identification R⊗C≃C performs scalar multiplication; the definition works without a basis, finite-dimensionality, or multiplication on C. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficient_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L82), [counit_matrixCoefficient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L160).
Evaluation applies the functional to the vector factor of the coaction.
Counit evaluation recovers the original functional value.

The coefficient c(φ,m) is the element Σφ(m₀)m₁ of the coefficient coalgebra. For coordinate functionals and basis vectors these are exactly the matrix entries of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). This is an element of C, not a scalar until evaluated; its value depends on the specified coaction, even when φ and m are unchanged. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficient_groupLike](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L205), [matrixCoefficient_trivial](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L223).
A homogeneous coaction gives φ(m) times its group-like coefficient.
The trivial coaction gives φ(m) times the unit coefficient.

Evaluating the coefficient linear map attached to φ at m gives the coefficient element c(φ,m). This connects the bundled linear map with the concrete entry construction of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). No finite basis is assumed: the displayed equation records two presentations of the same contraction of the given right coaction. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficient_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L82), [matrixCoefficientTensor_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L135).
The element is explicitly the functional contraction of the coaction.
The tensor presentation gives the same value on φ⊗m.

The defining formula contracts the vector factor of ρ(m) with φ and then identifies R⊗C with C. Thus c(φ,m)=Σφ(m₀)m₁, yielding the coordinate entries in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The scalar factor acts on C through its module structure; it is not discarded, and no basis or decomposition is chosen. Checks pass: [counit_matrixCoefficient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L160), [matrixCoefficient_groupLike](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L205).
The formula recovers φ(m) after applying the counit.
For ρ(m)=m⊗g, the formula gives φ(m)•g.

For fixed φ, the coefficient of m+n is the sum of the two coefficients, because the coaction, tensor map and scalar-unit identification are linear. This extends the coordinate construction in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) to arbitrary vectors. It is ordinary module additivity, with no finite-dimensionality or coalgebra multiplication required. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficient_zero](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L89), [matrixCoefficient_add_functional](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L147).
The same linear map sends the zero vector to zero.
The complementary functional-variable additivity confirms bilinearity.

Scaling the vector by r scales its coefficient by r, since each step of the coefficient contraction is R-linear. This is the scalar compatibility of the entries underlying [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Scalars act through the module structure of C; the statement works over a commutative semiring, without requiring inverses or a field. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficient_smul_functional](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L154), [matrixCoefficient_trivial](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L223).
Scaling the functional produces the same scalar factor.
The trivial coaction specializes the coefficient to the ordinary functional evaluation times 1.

The coefficient pairing is linear separately in φ and m, packaged as a linear map from the dual into linear maps M→C. This is the bilinear contraction underlying the coordinate entries of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The dual means R-linear functionals; no complex conjugation, inner product, or finite-dimensional identification with a double dual is used. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientBilinear_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L123), [matrixCoefficient_add_functional](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L147).
Evaluation of the packaged bilinear map is exactly c(φ,m).
Additivity in the functional is verified directly.

Bilinearity of c(φ,m) gives a linear map M*⊗M→C sending φ⊗m to that coefficient. This packages the coefficient entries of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) without choosing a basis. Tensor balancing identifies (rφ)⊗m with φ⊗(rm); the construction does not assert that this map is injective, surjective, or an identification with an endomorphism algebra. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientTensor_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L135), [matrixCoefficient_smul_functional](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L154).
The descended map has the prescribed value on elementary tensors.
The functional scalar rule agrees with the vector scalar rule needed for balancing.

On the elementary tensor φ⊗m, the coefficient tensor map evaluates to c(φ,m). This is the universal-property formula for the bilinear contraction underlying [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). It determines the map by linearity, while leaving general tensors as sums; it does not assert that every tensor is elementary or that the coefficient map is an isomorphism. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientBilinear_apply_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L123), [counit_matrixCoefficient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L160).
The bilinear map being lifted has exactly this value.
Counit evaluation of this value gives the usual pairing φ(m).

Scaling φ by r scales c(φ,m) by r because tensoring and the scalar-unit identification are linear in the functional. This is the dual-variable scalar rule for the coefficient construction in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The dual here is algebraic and linear, so the scalar is unchanged rather than complex-conjugated. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficient_add_functional](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L147), [matrixCoefficient_groupLike](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L205).
The functional variable also preserves addition.
For a homogeneous coaction the formula reduces to scaling φ(m)•g.

Applying ε to c(φ,m) returns φ(m), by contracting the comodule counit identity with φ. With coordinate functionals this is the identity-matrix condition ε(aᵢⱼ)=δᵢⱼ in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The general statement needs no basis and uses the coalgebra counit, which becomes evaluation at the group identity in the coordinate-algebra interpretation. Checks pass: [counit_coefficientMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L99), [matrixCoefficient_counit_self](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L194).
Basis-coordinate coefficients give the Kronecker delta.
For the regular comodule, contraction with its counit recovers the element itself.

For a comodule morphism f:M→N, taking the coefficient of f(m) with φ equals taking the coefficient of m with φ∘f. Compatibility of f with the coactions proves this naturality of the construction in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The map f need not be invertible; ordinary linearity alone would not ensure the identity. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficientHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Morphism.lean#L86), [counit_matrixCoefficient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L160).
The coefficient operation is realized by an actual morphism to the regular comodule.
Counit evaluation on both sides gives the same composite functional value.

On the regular comodule C, whose coaction is Δ, the coefficient attached to ε is the original element: Σ ε(c₁)c₂=c. This is the coalgebra counit identity applied to the coefficient construction of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The regular carrier need not have a finite basis, and the result requires no Hopf antipode. Checks pass: [matrixCoefficient_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L82), [counit_matrixCoefficient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L160).
The coefficient contracts the first factor of Δ with ε.
Applying the remaining counit gives ε(c), consistently with the general evaluation law.

The coproduct of c(φ,m) is obtained by coacting on m and applying the coefficient map c(φ,−) to its vector factor. Coassociativity gives this basis-free version of the matrix coproduct identity in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Its ordered output lies in C⊗C; neither a finite basis nor cocommutativity is assumed. Checks pass: [comul_matrixCoefficient_eq_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Comul.lean#L135), [matrixCoefficientHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Morphism.lean#L78).
A finite basis expands this identity into the ordered coefficient sum.
The same identity equips the coefficient map with regular-comodule compatibility.

For a finite basis eᵢ with coordinate functionals eⁱ, the coaction expands as ρ(m)=Σeᵢ⊗c(eⁱ,m). This recovers its actual tensor from the coefficient entries of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Finiteness is supplied by the basis index type, rather than inferred from a generic dimension value; no basis of the coefficient coalgebra is needed. Checks pass: [coact_basis_eq_sum_coefficientMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L109), [comul_matrixCoefficient_eq_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Comul.lean#L135).
Basis-vector specialization gives the corresponding matrix column.
The expansion produces the expected finite sum for the coproduct.

With a finite basis eᵢ, the coproduct is Δc(φ,m)=Σc(φ,eᵢ)⊗c(eⁱ,m). Coassociativity and the basis expansion prove the ordered formula underlying [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The first coefficient uses φ and the basis vector; the second uses its coordinate functional and m, so reversing the tensor factors would change the statement. Checks pass: [comul_matrixCoefficient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Comul.lean#L57), [comul_coefficientMatrix_eq_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L115).
The basis-free identity fixes the order of the two factors.
Coordinate functionals and basis vectors specialize it to matrix multiplication.

The (i,j) entry is c(eⁱ,eⱼ): row i selects the output coordinate and column j selects the input basis vector. This is the coefficient matrix of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The definition permits an arbitrary basis index type; finite matrix sums and determinants are introduced only by later results with explicit finiteness hypotheses. Checks pass: [coact_basis_eq_sum_coefficientMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L109), [coefficientMatrix_basisFun](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/StandardComodule.lean#L102).
For a finite basis, the jth coaction is precisely the jth matrix column.
For the standard general-linear comodule this is the generic matrix.

The entry formula identifies aᵢⱼ with the coefficient of basis vector eⱼ against coordinate functional eⁱ, matching [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). This fixes the row and column convention without transposing the matrix. The equation is valid for arbitrary basis index types; it requires neither a finite sum nor multiplication in the coefficient coalgebra. Checks pass: [counit_coefficientMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L99), [coefficientMatrix_basisFun](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/StandardComodule.lean#L102).
The entry convention gives δᵢⱼ under the counit.
The standard representation confirms that the entries are the generic matrix coordinates.

Corestricting a coaction along f:C→D applies f entrywise to its coefficient matrix, with the same basis and carrier module. This follows by commuting f with the functional contraction defining the entries in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The direction is covariant in the coalgebra map; neither invertibility nor an algebra multiplication on C or D is needed. Checks pass: [corestrict_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L169), [counit_coefficientMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L99).
The changed coaction is exactly (id⊗f)ρ.
The resulting coefficients retain the identity-matrix counit condition.

Applying the counit to aᵢⱼ gives δᵢⱼ, since εc(eⁱ,eⱼ)=eⁱ(eⱼ). This is the second coefficient-matrix identity in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Decidable equality supplies the displayed choice between 1 and 0; the identity is entrywise and needs no finite index set or matrix multiplication. Checks pass: [counit_matrixCoefficient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L160), [map_counit_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L89).
The general functional/vector counit formula yields the entry value.
In the bialgebra setting these entrywise equations are exactly the matrix counit identity.

The coaction of eⱼ is Σeᵢ⊗aᵢⱼ, so its coefficients form column j rather than row j. This is exactly the finite-basis convention in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The finite sum ranges over the supplied basis index type; no coordinate matrix of an already evaluated group element is being substituted. Checks pass: [coact_eq_sum_basis_matrixCoefficient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Comul.lean#L125), [standardCoact_apply_basisFun](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/GeneralLinear/StandardComodule.lean#L74).
The general vector expansion specializes to eⱼ.
The standard general-linear coaction gives the corresponding column of the generic matrix.

The matrix entries satisfy Δ(aᵢⱼ)=Σₖaᵢₖ⊗aₖⱼ, precisely the first identity in [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). This is matrix multiplication across two tensor factors, derived from coassociativity. It holds over a coalgebra alone: the displayed summands are tensors, not products in C, and the basis index is explicitly finite. Checks pass: [comul_matrixCoefficient_eq_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Comul.lean#L135), [coefficientMatrix_matrixComodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/FromMatrix.lean#L202).
The general coefficient coproduct specializes to coordinate functionals.
Reconstruction from a matrix satisfying the coalgebra identities recovers that matrix.

For basis indices p,q, the sum ΣₓaₚₓS(aₓq) equals the scalar image of eᵖ(e_q), hence the identity-matrix entry. The coproduct expansion turns this directly into [EGNO, antipode axiom 1.22.1](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44). Multiplication remains in the displayed order; neither commutativity of C nor bijectivity of its antipode is required. Checks pass: [coefficientMatrix_mul_map_antipode](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L161), [sum_antipode_mul_matrixCoefficient_eq_algebraMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L149).
Packaging these entries gives the right-inverse matrix equation.
The companion antipode identity gives the opposite multiplication order.

The coefficient matrix A multiplied by its entrywise antipode transform S(A) is the identity. Each entry follows from [EGNO, antipode axiom 1.22.1](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44) applied to Δ(aᵢⱼ), then the counit identity. S is applied entrywise without transposing A; the result is valid for noncommutative Hopf coefficient semirings and does not require an inverse map for S. Checks pass: [sum_matrixCoefficient_mul_antipode_eq_algebraMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L138), [map_antipode_mul_coefficientMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L172).
The entrywise sum gives exactly the Kronecker-delta scalar image.
The same entrywise antipode transform is also a left inverse.

The finite coefficient matrix has entrywise antipode inverse, by [EGNO, antipode axiom 1.22.1](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=44); multiplicativity of determinants therefore makes det(A) a unit in the commutative coefficient ring. Unit means multiplicatively invertible; nonzero alone does not suffice over general rings. The empty-basis case gives determinant 1, and the statement also correctly includes the zero ring. Checks pass: [coefficientMatrix_mul_map_antipode](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L161), [map_antipode_mul_coefficientMatrix](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Matrix.lean#L172).
An explicit right inverse supplies determinant invertibility.
The same matrix also gives the left-inverse identity.

A real number is an equivalence class of rational Cauchy sequences: two sequences represent the same number when their difference tends to zero. Lean wraps this quotient in a separate type. Equality concerns the limiting value, so distinct sequences can define the same real number; no preferred approximation sequence is selected. Compared with [Kiming, §2.2](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L36).

Real zero is the class of the constant rational sequence 0,0,…, serving as the additive identity. Every rational Cauchy sequence tending to zero represents this same element, even when none of its terms is zero. Thus the representation is an entire equivalence class, not a uniquely stored sequence. Compared with [Kiming, Theorem1](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L90).

Real one is the class of the constant rational sequence 1,1,… and is the multiplicative identity for the usual real arithmetic. It is distinct from zero. Other Cauchy sequences approaching one represent the same element, so this construction fixes a number rather than a unique sequence of approximations. Compared with [Kiming, Theorem1](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L94).

Addition of real numbers is induced by termwise addition of rational Cauchy representatives. Replacing either sequence by an equivalent one leaves the resulting real number unchanged. The operation therefore adds their represented values exactly, including negative and irrational values; it does not add a fixed finite number of decimal digits. Compared with [Kiming, Definition5](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L98).

Negating a real number negates every term of a rational Cauchy representative and then takes its equivalence class. This is the additive inverse, so negative inputs become positive and zero stays zero. The result is independent of the representative; it is not absolute value or a truncation to nonnegative numbers. Compared with [Kiming, §§2.1–2.2](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L102).

Multiplication of real numbers comes from termwise multiplication of rational Cauchy sequences. Cauchy sequences are bounded, which ensures their products remain Cauchy and equivalent representatives give the same product. The resulting operation is exact for all real inputs, including irrational values; it is neither a convolution nor multiplication of decimal strings. Compared with [Kiming, Definition5](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L106).

Real subtraction is defined by x−y=x+(−y), using the usual additive inverse. It is signed subtraction: for example, 3−5 is −2, not zero. This differs from natural-number subtraction, which truncates at zero. Passing to equivalent Cauchy representatives preserves the represented real difference. Compared with [Kiming, §§2.1–2.2](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L109).

The reciprocal of a nonzero real number is represented by reciprocals of a Cauchy representative, whose terms eventually stay away from zero. Lean additionally defines the reciprocal of zero to be zero. Thus x·x⁻¹=1 still requires x≠0; zero is not assigned an infinite value or a multiplicative inverse. Compared with [Kiming, Theorem1](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L113).

A natural number n becomes the real number represented by the constant rational sequence n,n,… . The conversion preserves its exact nonnegative integer value. It happens after any operations already performed in the natural numbers: casting an existing natural result does not change the arithmetic that produced that result. Compared with [Kiming, Proposition8](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L161).

An integer is included in the reals by its constant rational Cauchy sequence. Negative integers keep their sign, and zero and positive integers keep their ordinary values. This is an exact inclusion, rather than a conversion to a natural number; no truncation, absolute value or numerical approximation is applied. Compared with [Kiming, Proposition8](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L162).

A nonnegative rational number is included in the reals with its exact fractional value. For example, 5/2 as a nonnegative rational becomes the real number 2.5; this conversion does not perform natural-number floor division. The domain excludes negative rationals, while allowing zero and every nonnegative rational fraction. Compared with [Kiming, Proposition8](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L163).

Every rational number is included in the reals by its constant Cauchy sequence, preserving signed fractional values exactly. Thus −5/2 becomes −2.5, rather than an integer quotient or a rounded approximation. This cast includes negative rationals as well as zero; the separate nonnegative-rational cast has a smaller domain. Compared with [Kiming, Proposition8](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L164).

The real arithmetic induced from rational Cauchy sequences forms a commutative ring: addition and multiplication are associative and commutative, multiplication distributes over addition, and every element has an additive inverse. The source retains the previously defined operations and integer inclusions. This package establishes ring laws; reciprocals and order are supplied separately. Compared with [Kiming, Theorem1](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L176).

The constructed real numbers form a field with their existing addition, multiplication and reciprocal. Every nonzero number has a multiplicative inverse. Lean makes division total by assigning 0⁻¹=0, so division by zero returns zero and cancellation still needs a nonzero denominator. The field package alone does not assert order completeness. Compared with [Kiming, Theorem1](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L481).

For real numbers represented by sequences a and b, a<b means that bₙ−aₙ is eventually at least a fixed positive rational amount. Merely having aₙ<bₙ at every stage is insufficient: 1/(n+1) stays positive but represents zero. The positive-gap condition makes strict order independent of the chosen representatives. Compared with [Kiming, §3.1](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L266).

The nonstrict order on real numbers is defined by x≤y exactly when x<y or x=y, using the quotient’s equality and strict order. It therefore includes equality even when two representatives cross repeatedly. Eventual termwise comparison is sufficient, but it is not the definition of comparison between represented real numbers. Compared with [Kiming, §3.1](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L297).

The usual real comparison is reflexive, transitive and antisymmetric. Antisymmetry here means equality of represented real numbers, not equality of their approximation sequences. Passing to equivalence classes is essential: at the sequence level, comparison in both directions only says the difference tends to zero. Total comparability is established separately. Compared with [Kiming, §3.1](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L313).

The real numbers carry a linear order: any two numbers are comparable, and strict comparison, equality and the reverse strict comparison give the usual trichotomy. Lean retains the already constructed order and minimum/maximum operations. Its comparison decisions use classical reasoning; this structure does not provide an executable algorithm for comparing arbitrary real inputs. Compared with [Kiming, Proposition9](https://web.math.ku.dk/~kiming/papers/2020_real_numbers/real_numbers_supervisor.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L471).

The maximum of two real numbers is the larger one, with equal inputs returning that same value. The source constructs it by taking pointwise maxima of rational Cauchy representatives and then their equivalence class. This yields the least upper bound of the pair; it does not assert that arbitrary sets have a maximum. Compared with [Faris, §§5.3–5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L375).

The minimum of two real numbers is the smaller one, including when both are equal or negative. It is obtained from pointwise minima of rational Cauchy representatives, independently of representative choices. The result is the greatest lower bound of this two-element set; there is no requirement that the inputs be nonnegative. Compared with [Faris, §§5.3–5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean#L391).

For finite measures μ,ν of equal mass and bounded measurable g, bounded measurable φ,ψ make exp(φ(x)+ψ(y)+g(x,y)) a density against μ⊗ν whose two marginals are μ,ν. Lean’s conversion to nonnegative extended reals preserves this positive exponential. No topology is assumed; for g=0 and common mass m>0 the density is 1/m. See [Nutz, Theorem 2.1 and §2.1, pp.16–18](https://www.math.columbia.edu/~mnutz/docs/EOT_lecture_notes.pdf); the [bounded-kernel contraction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Entropic/SchroedingerSystem.lean#L369) supplies the stated generality. Checks pass: [product reference](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Entropic/Basic.lean#L170) and [exact 2×2 family](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Data/Matrix/Scaling/Basic.lean#L327).
The probability product-reference calibration has value0, witnessed by the actual product coupling.
The computed product family supplies the exact 2×2 matrix scaling with entries1/2 and the two prescribed margins.

Finitely many probability laws on the real line with finite second moments and nonnegative weights summing to one have exactly one minimizer of the weighted sum of squared W₂ distances. Its quantile is almost everywhere the weighted average of input quantiles. Atomic inputs and zero weights are allowed; “two” denotes the squared-distance exponent. See [Agueh–Carlier, §6.1, pp.18–19 (nonatomic case)](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~carlier/AC_bary_Aug11_10.pdf). Native Checks pass: [averaged quantiles](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Barycenter/Basic.lean#L108), [Dirac quantiles](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Probability/Distributions/Dirac.lean#L64) with [base variance](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Group/WeightedVariance.lean#L36), and [two-law geodesics](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Barycenter/Basic.lean#L312) with [barycentric interpolation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Barycenter/Basic.lean#L352) and [quadratic weight-time](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/FrechetMean/TwoPoint.lean#L85).
The actual constructed law has the weighted-average quantile, not just an existence specification.
The native constant-quantile formula evaluates that computed family on Dirac inputs.
The same weighted base-space variance decomposition used inside the barycenter proof identifies the Dirac-input mean.
The actual two-law interpolants form a constant-speed Wasserstein geodesic.
The actual interpolant at the calculated barycentric time is a Fréchet barycenter.
At quadratic exponent the computed barycentric time equals the input weight.

On a proper metric space, finitely many laws μᵢ with finite p-th moments admit a minimizer of ΣwᵢWₚ(ν,μᵢ)^p for 1≤p<∞ and nonnegative weights totaling one. The Dirac masses δ_(μᵢ) in the statement are on the space of laws. Dirac inputs on the base space instead give its Fréchet objective, permitting mixtures of minimizing points. See [Le Gouic–Loubes, Lemma 7 and Theorem 8, pp.11–12](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.04153); their geodesicity hypothesis is unnecessary for the [native proper-space selection](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/FrechetMean/Selection.lean#L198). Checks pass: [arbitrary-law Dirac cost](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L514), [its integral formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Function/Lp/LIntegralRpow.lean#L48), [base Fréchet cost](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/FrechetMean/Basic.lean#L84), [pointwise minima](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/FrechetMean/Selection.lean#L198) and [mixture interpretation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/MultiMarginal/Barycenter.lean#L505).
The existing one-Dirac family computes the cost against every candidate probability law, not only against a Dirac candidate.
Under the actual finite nonzero exponent and measurability hypotheses, the one-Dirac cost raised to p is the integral of the base distance power.
The base finite-family Fréchet objective is exactly the finite weighted distance-power sum.
The base pointwise minimum is attained by the actual measurable selector.
The native converse gives the mixture-of-pointwise-minimizers interpretation, preserving possible nonuniqueness.
